en: The dyad of "dissociated from the taints and with taints" and the triad of "the wholesome."

Conditioned by a state that is dissociated from the taints (*āsava*), is neither non-tainted nor wholesome, a wholesome state that is dissociated from the taints and is non-tainted arises by way of root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*).

Conditioned by a state that is dissociated from the taints, is neither non-tainted nor wholesome, a wholesome state that is dissociated from the taints but is tainted (*sāsava*) arises by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated. Under root-condition...
Two ... [and so on] ... two non-disappeared conditions.

With a state that is dissociated from the taints (*āsava*), neither-tainted-nor-non-tainted, and not-unwholesome as condition, there arises a state that is dissociated from the taints, tainted, and unwholesome, by way of root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*). (Abbreviated. One under root-condition ... [and so on] ... one under non-disappearance condition.

Dependent on a state that is dissociated from the taints, neither-tainted-nor-non-tainted, and indeterminate (*avyākata*) ... [there arises] a state that is dissociated from the taints, tainted, and indeterminate.

A state arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a state that is dissociated from the taints, is neither with-taint nor indeterminate, there arises a state that is dissociated from the taints, is with-taint, and is indeterminate, by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. There are two under root;
two under predominance … pe … two under non-disappearance.
